name: Veterinary clinics (category guide)
summary: AVS-licensed vets for post-import pets — licence clocks, emergency vs GP clinics, and why relocation agents are not your ongoing clinic.
body: After CAPQ and the relocation agent handoff, you still need a neighbourhood veterinary clinic for vaccines, parasite control, and emergencies. Confirm the practice is licensed under NParks / Animal & Veterinary Service (AVS) rules — Facebook ‘house-call only’ vendors are a recurring risk. Budget for higher cash fees than many home countries; pet insurance sold overseas often excludes Singapore clinics or waits out pre-existing conditions. Ask about after-hours coverage before the first fever at 11pm — not every GP vet runs a 24-hour emergency bench. Keep import vaccination and rabies-serology originals; clinics will not reinvent CAPQ paperwork from memory. Licensing and sterilisation rules for dogs/cats sit with AVS and your town council / condo by-laws — clinic advice does not override estate pet clauses. Pair this directory entry with the pet-relocation category guide for import, and with daily-life pet guidance for housing and transit. This is a category guide, not a ranked vet list. Pet imaging (X-ray / ultrasound) is a separate cash quote from the consult — ask for imaging line items up front the same way human diagnostic imaging is itemised in the radiology category guide.
whenToEngage: Post-import pet needs local GP vet relationship
Overseas pet insurance may not pay Singapore clinics
Need AVS-aligned vaccine / licence paperwork continuity
Need pet X-ray / ultrasound quote before agreeing
